episodes.180532: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved through Central New York throughout daytime hours. Many storms became severe with strong wind gusts being the main hazard. Two NWS surveys confirmed strong microbursts. Both microbursts resulted in widespread damage that included damage to structures. Unfortunately on this day, three roofers were struck by lightning after taking shelter under a tree while waiting for a storm to pass. One of them succumbed to their injuries a few days after the incident.
episodes.181115: A dying thunderstorm produced a dry microburst that spread out across eastern Colfax and western Union Counties on July 23rd. This produced a severe wind gust that blew through Capulin breaking tree branches up to 6 inches in diameter and blew over a shed.
episodes.181149: On the afternoon of the 23rd, a departing mesoscale convective vortex promoted a rotating, marginally-severe thunderstorm that slowly crossed the Muncie area.  Mainly scattered strong cells developed along the Interstate 70 corridor soon after, with isolated wind damage in central Owen County.||During the late evening another cluster of strong thunderstorms developed over east-central Illinois, tracking through southwestern central Indiana very early on the 24th, with isolated wind damage occurring in northern Owen County.
episodes.181150: A very unstable atmosphere with upwards of 3000 J/kg of CAPE combined with an approaching upper wave to produce several large and slow-moving afternoon thunderstorms over mainly eastern central Indiana.  A few severe storms produced large hail and wind damage, including 1.50 inch hail over the eastern Indianapolis Metro, and a flattened large barn in Henry County.
episodes.181201: In the midst of hot and muggy conditions ruling the roost over the Central Appalachians, diurnally driven showers and thunderstorms thrived near the end of July. On the afternoon of July 24th, a few storms that originated in southeast Ohio crossed over the river into West Virginia. One particular storm that passed over Wood County resulted in strong damaging winds that day and caused downed trees in and around the Parkersburg area. Locally heavy downpours also resulted in a small creek to rise out of its banks briefly in the town of Mineral Wells.
episodes.181360: After high pressure dominated western Colorado for several days, moisture gradually increased ahead of an approaching system. This led to the development of isolated to scattered high-based thunderstorms. Given the dry air at the lower levels, gusty outflow winds were the primary threat from storms. The stronger storms produced gusty winds in excess of 58 mph across Moffat County.
episodes.181463: Showers and thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain to Berks County during the late afternoon and early evening of July 24.  Rainfall totals were as high as 1 to 2 inches.
episodes.181592: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed over central Pennsylvania during the early afternoon hours, with a couple of cells producing wind damage. Storms eventually coalesced into a broken line of discrete cells that crossed the Susquehanna Valley during the evening hours, producing sporadic wind damage.
episodes.181609: A sharp low pressure trough crossed western New York in the afternoon. Thunderstorms first occurred along the Niagara Frontier lake breeze convergence zone with additional clusters of thunderstorms later across the Finger Lakes to the eastern Lake Ontario region. Multiple reports of wind damage were received. An additional round of thunderstorms crossed the Niagara River later in the evening and produced wind damage near Youngstown.
episodes.181610: A sharp low pressure trough crossed western New York in the afternoon. Thunderstorms first occurred along the Niagara Frontier lake breeze convergence zone with additional clusters of thunderstorms later across the Finger Lakes to the eastern Lake Ontario region. Multiple reports of wind damage were received. An additional round of thunderstorms crossed the Niagara River later in the evening and produced wind damage near Youngstown.
episodes.181690: Strong to severe thunderstorms associated with shortwave troughs erupted over eastern New York during the afternoon hours on July 24th and July 25th resulting in multiple reports of downed trees and wires.
episodes.181752: Thunderstorms developed along a cold front across north-central Wisconsin during the afternoon hours on Monday (7/24).  The strongest storm produced penny size hail.
episodes.181815: Isolated thunderstorms occurred during the overnight and wee morning hours. One of the storms produced some tree damage in western Franklin County. The storms occurred in a weak southwest wind flow ahead of a cold front that trailed from Lake Michigan to central Missouri.
episodes.181817: Clusters of intense thunderstorm cells rapidly formed in a strongly unstable air mass during the heat of the afternoon. The most intense cells merged into a small severe thunderstorm complex around the northern end of the Land Between The Lakes area (Kentucky Lake and Lake Barkley). This complex was associated with sporadic large hail and damaging winds from southern Livingston County eastward across Lyon and Caldwell Counties. The storms occurred ahead of a slow-moving weak cold front that extended from central Indiana to the Ozarks of southwest Missouri.
episodes.181822: Thunderstorms rapidly formed in a strongly unstable air mass during the heat of the afternoon. The storms organized into a line of storms over extreme southeast Missouri for a brief time. A couple of the storms produced damaging winds and a brief tornado. The storms occurred ahead of a slow-moving weak cold front that extended from central Indiana to the Ozarks of southwest Missouri.
episodes.181892: A couple of thunderstorms produced localized wind damage over the eastern West Virginia panhandle.
episodes.182039: A trough pushes through the Nature Coast and West Central Florida following the longwave pattern. This helped to enhance the already moisture and unstable southwest to westerly flow. This resulted in numerous strong marine wind gusts once again.
episodes.182057: A weak surface boundary resulted in scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening. These storms resulted in numerous severe hail reports, the largest of which was 2.5 inches in Chatham, Illinois.
episodes.182160: Although the best forcing for severe weather was to our west over New York state, scattered diurnal thunderstorms formed over southern New England.  One caused some street flooding in northwest MA and one reached severe limits in northeast MA.
episodes.182346: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and evening hours as an upper level low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.182348: Scattered thunderstorms developed as a low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.182349: Scattered thunderstorms developed as a low pressure system moved through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.182529: Scattered showers and thunderstorms affected portions of eastern New York during the afternoon and early evening hours of July 24. A few storms produced heavy rainfall, leading to isolated reports of flash flooding in Essex County, NY.
episodes.182564: Strong thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts along the coast.
episodes.182615: Multiple rounds of thunderstorms moved through Northeastern Pennsylvania from the late morning hours through the evening on the 24th. episodes.182827: A line of storms developed in southern South Dakota and northern Nebraska and moved southeast into Iowa. Initially, storms produced large hail with the largest stones reported at 2.5 inches in Knox County. The storms produced hail across a few counties before eventually transitioning into a wind threat. A 67-mph wind gust was measured at Eppley Airfield but there were no reports of damage across the city of Omaha.
episodes.182904: An upper level storm system crossed the region during peak heating. The passage of this system aided in the lift needed for thunderstorm development within an already very moist and unstable atmosphere. The environment spawned scattered severe thunderstorms which produced damaging winds. In addition, storms were at times slow-moving, with winds up to 700 mb averaging around 10 knots from the southwest. Surface-based CAPEs across central Virginia varied from 1,500 to over 2,000 J/Kg during late afternoon, while precipitable water values varied from 1.2 inches across the Mountain Empire to 1.6 inches across the Southside area of Virginia.  The high instability and abundant atmospheric moisture combined to produce storms with high rainfall rates, at times observed to be up to 5 inches per hour.
episodes.182905: An upper level storm system crossed the region during peak heating. The passage of this system aided in the lift needed for thunderstorm development within an already very moist and unstable atmosphere. The environment spawned a couple of severe thunderstorms which produced damaging winds.
episodes.182978: A cluster of storms moved south-southeast across northwest Kansas just after midnight. A single gust of 58 mph was recorded in Colby.
episodes.182999: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183183: With a mid-level ridge over South Florida, there was just enough low-level moisture and daytime heating to develop several thunderstorms around Lake Okeechobee on the afternoon and evening of July 24th.
episodes.183239: Lingering mid-level moisture trapped under high pressure aloft fueled spotty thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. Isolated high winds occurred.
episodes.183240: Lingering mid-level moisture trapped under high pressure aloft fueled spotty thunderstorms over southern Nevada. Isolated high winds occurred.
episodes.183338: A high wind gust was recorded at Cameron from a thunderstorm.
episodes.183363: A cluster of thunderstorms formed over Ohio during the late afternoon and early evening hours of July 24th, as weak disturbances aloft sparked convection in an unstable atmosphere. The slow-moving storms impacted Coshocton County most keenly with wind damage and flash flooding.
episodes.183406: A few isolated thunderstorms developed over the region during the afternoon hours with daytime heating. Most of the storms remained well below severe limits, but one storm over Douglas County did produce penny-sized hail as it moved through.
episodes.183529: Sufficient moisture continued to flow through the region in late July, leading to daytime convection most days. This convection was occasionally strong to severe, yielding localized strong wind gusts in addition to flash flooding.
episodes.183658: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west across southeast Arizona during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorm winds caused extensive damage in southwest Tucson and on the Pascua Yaqui Pueblo.
episodes.183664: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved west across Pima County during the afternoon and evening. Thunderstorm winds caused extensive damage in Ajo.
episodes.183703: Isolated thunderstorms developed along the sea breeze in the late afternoon hours. One thunderstorm near Tybee Island produced strong wind gusts.
episodes.183783: Severe thunderstorms produced very strong wind gusts over parts of Adams, Denver and Weld counties.  Peak gusts ranged from 60 to 70 mph.
episodes.183796: An isolated thunderstorm resulted in a couple of severe wind gust reports.
episodes.183890: A weak wave produced a brief enhancement in mid-level warm advection, and with around 1000 J/kg elevated CAPE and marginal shear, a few storms developed with broad rotation and resulted in spotty large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183891: A weak wave produced a brief enhancement in mid-level warm advection, and with around 1000 J/kg elevated CAPE and marginal shear, a few storms developed with broad rotation and resulted in spotty large hail and damaging wind gusts.
episodes.183945: There were two areas of severe thunderstorms this day. Around Rock Springs, high based thunderstorms moved into an area with an almost 60 degree dew point depression. A maximum wind gust of 62 mph occurred at the Sweetwater County airport. A line of thunderstorms associated with a shortwave also moved into Teton County. A 61 mph wind gust was reported at the Jackson Hole airport. In Wilson, many trees were downed, resulting in the loss of power for several hours.
episodes.184111: A mid atmospheric disturbance moved across an unstable air mass across northern New York which led to scattered thunderstorms moving across the area. A few of these storm produced localized damaging winds.
episodes.184114: A mid atmospheric disturbance moved across an unstable air mass across NY which led to scattered thunderstorms moving across the area with one storm producing isolated damage in VT.
episodes.184191: Numerous thunderstorms formed over interior northern Michigan during the afternoon as lake breezes pushed inland from the Lake Michigan shoreline. One of these storms produced damaging wind gusts in Missaukee county.
episodes.184245: Monsoon moisture continued to move northward over northern Arizona with more thunderstorms developing.
episodes.184272: Thunderstorm damage and severe wind gusts in the Pocatello area.
episodes.184378: Isolated severe storms impacted much of the Upper Mississippi River Valley from the late afternoon into the early evening hours of July 24th. While nearly all storms weakened as they progressed into southeast Minnesota, one storm retained its severity and dropped half dollar sized hail near Rice Lake (Dodge County).
episodes.184396: Scattered thunderstorms associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced heavy rain which caused flash flooding across portions of southeast Virginia.
episodes.184397: Isolated severe thunderstorm associated with low pressure and a surface trough produced damaging winds across portions of northeast North Carolina.
episodes.184416: While the synoptic scale pattern on July 24th and 25th, 2023 had a similar appearance to earlier events in the month with large scale troughing across the Ohio Valley, the flow aloft was generally weaker, which limited the overall severe potential to more of a typical summertime event. On the other hand, instability values were quite impressive, with 2500-3500 J/kg of mixed-layer CAPE developing across central Kentucky and southern Indiana during the afternoon hours on July 24th. Convection initiated in the vicinity of a weak surface frontal boundary across southwestern Indiana and southern Illinois during the early afternoon hours, with storms moving off to the east and southeast along with the background flow aloft. The parameter space was generally favorable for ordinary cell thunderstorms, with a few multicell clusters also developing along and ahead of the front. The primary observed severe hazard was damaging straight-line winds, as between 1000-1400 J/kg of downdraft CAPE was observed on mesoanalysis data. Additionally, a couple instances of severe hail were also observed in southern Indiana, where significant hail parameter values were slightly higher (around or above 1). Storms gradually subsided after sunset on July 24th, with conditions remaining quiet through the morning and early afternoon hours on July 25th. While slightly drier air moved into southern Indiana and north central Kentucky and limited thunderstorm potential on July 25th, a few strong to severe storms developed across southern and southwestern Kentucky during the afternoon and evening hours. One of these storms was strong enough to produce severe hail near Burkesville in Cumberland County, Kentucky..

The core of a severe thunderstorm descended right onto Cayuga Lake around |224 PM EDT on July 24, 2023, blasting the immediate eastern shore with a |microburst of 70 to 80 mph winds at Union Springs. Numerous trees had |large branches snapped and a few were uprooted right at the edge of the |lake, also causing downed wires and a power pole. At least two houses, |and one shed, sustained moderate roof damage from large branches falling |on them. Several others had more cosmetic or minor damage from small |branches. There were also downed trees, a broken metal sign, and minor |boat damage at a marina. The property manager there even observed a |miniature seiche of sorts, with the power of the wind causing water to |surge a bit into the marina during the storm, then it flowed back out |shortly after.

A brief EF-2 tornado struck a homestead near the community of Bertrand in Scott County, MO. The tornado started on County Highway 532 just west of the intersection of Highway O. The tornado shifted and damaged several grain bins and destroyed two barns. A person in a truck nearby had their vehicle partially lifted briefly by the tornado. After crossing Highway O, the tornado severely damaged a house and adjacent auxiliary home, removing the roofs and collapsing some exterior walls of both buildings. Two people suffered minor injuries in the primary residence when they were cut by flying debris. After damaging some trees behind the buildings, the tornado dissipated as it moved into an agricultural field east of the residences. Peak winds were estimated near 115 mph.
